q.q: A device used to store electric charge is a:
q.e: A capacitor stores charge (and energy) between two plates separated by an insulator.

q.q: A gold leaf electroscope is used to:
q.e: The leaves spread apart when charged, showing the presence of charge.

q.q: Two capacitors of 2 microfarad and 3 microfarad are connected in parallel. The total capacitance is:
q.e: In parallel, capacitances simply add: 2 + 3 = 5 microfarad.

q.q: Lightning conductors on tall buildings are useful because they:
o: safely conduct charge to the earth
q.e: The metal rod gives charge an easy path to the ground, protecting the building.

q.q: Electric field lines point:
q.e: By convention, field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges.

q.q: Hazard of static electricity during fuel filling is reduced by:
q.e: Earthing lets charge flow away safely, so no spark forms near the fuel.

q.q: The SI unit of electric current is:
q.e: Current is measured in amperes (A). 1 A = 1 C of charge per second.

q.q: A current of 2 A flows through a 10 ohm resistor. The potential difference across it is:
q.e: Ohm's law: V = I x R = 2 x 10 = 20 V.

q.q: Three 6 ohm resistors are connected in parallel. The total resistance is:
q.e: For equal resistors in parallel, R = R/n = 6/3 = 2 ohm.

q.q: Household appliances are connected in parallel so that:
o: current is the same in all
each gets the full voltage and works independently
q.e: In parallel each appliance gets the mains voltage and can be switched on or off without affecting others.

q.q: A 100 W bulb is used for 10 hours. The energy used is:
q.e: Energy = power x time = 0.1 kW x 10 h = 1 kWh (one unit on the electricity bill).

q.q: A fuse protects a circuit by:
o: melting and breaking the circuit when current is too high
q.e: The thin fuse wire melts when current exceeds its rating, cutting off the supply.

q.q: An ammeter is connected in a circuit:
q.e: An ammeter measures the current through a component, so it must be in series. A voltmeter goes in parallel.

q.q: The resistance of a metal wire increases when:
q.e: R is proportional to length and inversely proportional to area; for metals it also rises with temperature.

q.q: The earth wire in a plug is connected to the:
q.e: If a fault makes the metal body live, current flows to earth, blowing the fuse and protecting the user.

q.q: Electricity costs Rs 50 per unit. Running a 2 kW heater for 3 hours costs:
q.e: Energy = 2 kW x 3 h = 6 kWh = 6 units. Cost = 6 x 50 = Rs 300.

q.q: A current-carrying wire produces around it a:
q.e: Oersted showed that electric current produces a magnetic field around the wire.

q.q: The direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire is found by the:
q.e: Grip the wire with the right hand, thumb along the current: the fingers curl in the field direction.

q.q: An electric motor converts:
q.e: A motor uses the force on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field to produce rotation.

q.q: An AC generator converts:
q.e: Rotating a coil in a magnetic field induces an emf (electromagnetic induction).

q.q: Producing an emf by changing the magnetic field through a coil is called:
q.e: Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction; a changing magnetic flux induces emf.

q.q: A transformer has 100 turns in the primary and 500 in the secondary. With 220 V input, the output is:
q.e: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, so Vs = 220 x 500/100 = 1100 V. This is a step-up transformer.

q.q: Transformers work only with:
q.e: A transformer needs a changing magnetic field, which only AC provides.

q.q: Electricity is transmitted over long distances at very high voltage to:
o: reduce energy loss in the wires
q.e: Higher voltage means lower current for the same power, so less energy is lost as heat (I squared R).

q.q: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by:
q.e: More turns, more current and a soft iron core all make a stronger electromagnet.

q.q: The direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by:
q.e: Fleming's left hand rule: First finger Field, seCond finger Current, thuMb Motion (force).

q.q: Electrons are emitted from a heated metal surface. This is called:
q.e: Heating gives electrons enough energy to escape the metal surface.

q.q: A signal whose value changes continuously is called:
q.e: Analogue signals vary smoothly (like a sound wave); digital signals have only fixed levels such as 0 and 1.

q.q: The output of an AND gate is 1 only when:
q.e: AND gives 1 only if every input is 1.

q.q: A NOT gate:
o: gives the same output as input
q.e: NOT changes 1 to 0 and 0 to 1.

q.q: The output of an OR gate is 0 only when:
q.e: OR gives 1 if any input is 1, so it is 0 only when every input is 0.

q.q: A NAND gate is equivalent to:
o: an AND gate followed by a NOT gate
a NOT gate followed by an OR gate
q.e: NAND = NOT AND; its output is the opposite of AND.

q.q: In a cathode ray oscilloscope (CRO), electrons are deflected using:
q.e: Deflecting plates create electric fields that move the electron beam on the screen.

q.q: In binary, the number 5 is written as:
ICT stands for:
q.e: ICT covers technologies used to store, process and communicate information.

q.q: Optical fibres carry information as:
q.e: Information is sent as pulses of light, which reflect totally inside the fibre.

q.q: Which device stores data permanently even when power is off?
o: a hard disk or flash memory
q.e: Hard disks and flash drives keep data without power; RAM loses it.

q.q: Mobile phones communicate using:
q.e: Mobile phones send and receive signals as radio/microwaves through towers.

q.q: Which of these is a safe practice online?
o: Never sharing your password or OTP with anyone
Sharing OTP with a caller who says he is from the bank
Clicking every prize link on WhatsApp
q.e: Banks never ask for OTPs. Keeping passwords and OTPs private protects you from fraud.

q.q: The internet is best described as:
o: a worldwide network of connected computer networks
q.e: The internet links millions of networks around the world.

q.q: E-mail is a way of:
o: sending messages electronically over the internet
q.e: E-mail sends text and files between users over the internet.

q.q: A fax machine sends:
o: copies of documents over telephone lines
q.e: Fax scans a document and sends it as signals over telephone lines.

q.q: Alpha particles are:
q.e: An alpha particle has 2 protons and 2 neutrons, like a helium nucleus.

q.q: Which radiation has the greatest penetrating power?
q.e: Gamma rays are electromagnetic waves with no charge; they need thick lead or concrete to stop them.

q.q: Which radiation can be stopped by a sheet of paper?
q.e: Alpha particles are heavy and highly ionising, so they are stopped by paper or skin.

q.q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 2 days. After 6 days, the fraction left is:
q.e: 6 days = 3 half-lives. Fraction left = (1/2)^3 = 1/8.

q.q: When a nucleus emits a beta particle, its atomic number:
q.e: A neutron changes into a proton and an electron (beta). One more proton means atomic number + 1.

q.q: Radioisotopes are used in medicine to:
o: diagnose and treat diseases like cancer
q.e: Tracers help diagnosis and gamma rays are used in radiotherapy.

q.q: Background radiation comes from:
o: natural sources like rocks, soil and cosmic rays, plus some man-made sources
q.e: Most background radiation is natural: radon gas, rocks, cosmic rays and our own bodies.

q.q: Splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei is called:
q.e: Nuclear fission (for example uranium-235) releases a large amount of energy, used in nuclear power plants.

q.q: At chemical equilibrium:
o: the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal
q.e: Equilibrium is dynamic: both reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

q.q: A reaction that can go in both directions is called:
q.e: Reversible reactions are shown with a double arrow and can reach equilibrium.

q.q: For a reaction at equilibrium, a very large value of Kc means:
q.e: Kc = [products]/[reactants]; a large Kc means products are favoured.

q.q: Equilibrium can be reached only in a:
q.e: In an open system products can escape, so the reverse reaction cannot keep up.

q.q: In the reaction N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3, increasing the pressure:
o: shifts equilibrium towards nitrogen and hydrogen
q.e: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules: 2 on the right versus 4 on the left (Le Chatelier).

q.q: The law of mass action states that the rate of a reaction is proportional to the:
o: product of the active masses (concentrations) of the reactants
q.e: Rate is proportional to the product of reactant concentrations, each raised to its coefficient.

q.q: Adding a catalyst to a reaction at equilibrium:
o: does not change the equilibrium position but helps reach it faster
q.e: A catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally.

q.q: If Kc for a reaction is 0.001, at equilibrium the mixture contains:
q.e: A very small Kc means the reaction hardly proceeds forward.

q.q: According to Arrhenius, an acid produces in water:
q.e: Arrhenius acids give hydrogen ions (H+) in water; bases give hydroxide ions (OH-).

q.q: According to Bronsted-Lowry, a base is a:
q.e: Bronsted-Lowry: acids donate protons (H+), bases accept them.

q.q: A solution with pH 3 is:
q.e: pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.

q.q: Acid + base gives:
q.e: This is neutralisation, for example HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O.

q.q: Which of these is a strong acid?
q.e: HCl ionises completely in water, making it a strong acid. Acetic acid (vinegar) is weak.

q.q: A Lewis acid is a substance that:
q.e: Lewis acids accept electron pairs (for example BF3); Lewis bases donate them.

q.q: Phenolphthalein turns pink in:
q.e: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acid and pink in base.

q.q: An antacid tablet relieves acidity in the stomach because it is:
o: a mild base that neutralises excess acid
q.e: Antacids like magnesium hydroxide neutralise extra stomach acid (HCl).

q.q: Organic compounds always contain:
q.e: Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds (mostly with hydrogen).

q.q: Carbon can form long chains and rings. This property is called:
q.e: Catenation is the ability of carbon atoms to bond with each other in chains and rings.

q.q: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called:
q.e: Isomers have the same formula but different arrangement of atoms.

q.q: The functional group -OH is found in:
q.e: -OH is the hydroxyl group of alcohols, like ethanol C2H5OH.

q.q: The functional group -COOH is called:
q.e: Carboxylic acids such as acetic acid contain -COOH.

q.q: The main source of organic compounds such as fuels is:
q.e: Fossil fuels are the major source of hydrocarbons and many organic chemicals.

q.q: Members of a homologous series differ from each other by:
q.e: Each member differs from the next by -CH2-, and they share similar chemical properties.

q.q: Ethanol is commonly used as:
q.e: Ethanol is used as a solvent, in medicines and as a fuel.

q.q: Hydrocarbons are compounds of:
q.e: Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen atoms.

q.q: Alkanes have the general formula:
q.e: Alkanes are saturated: CnH2n+2 (methane CH4, ethane C2H6).

q.q: Ethene (C2H4) is an example of an:
q.e: Alkenes have a carbon-carbon double bond and the formula CnH2n.

q.q: Alkynes contain a:
q.e: Alkynes such as ethyne (acetylene) have a carbon-carbon triple bond: CnH2n-2.

q.q: Bromine water is decolourised by ethene but not by ethane because ethene is:
q.e: The double bond in ethene adds bromine, removing its colour. Ethane has no double bond.

q.q: Complete combustion of methane produces:
q.e: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, releasing heat. Incomplete combustion makes poisonous CO.

q.q: Natural gas (Sui gas) is mainly:
q.e: Natural gas used in Pakistani homes is mostly methane.

q.q: Burning gas heaters in a closed room is dangerous because they can produce:
q.e: In low oxygen, incomplete combustion gives colourless, odourless, poisonous CO. Always keep ventilation.

q.q: Carbohydrates are made of:
q.e: Carbohydrates like glucose (C6H12O6) contain C, H and O.

q.q: Glucose is an example of a:
q.e: Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide). Starch and cellulose are polysaccharides.

q.q: Proteins are made of:
q.e: Amino acids join by peptide bonds to make proteins.

q.q: The main function of fats and oils in our diet is to:
q.e: Lipids give more energy per gram than carbohydrates and store energy.

q.q: DNA and RNA are:
q.e: Nucleic acids carry genetic information.

q.q: Vitamin C deficiency causes:
q.e: Scurvy (bleeding gums) is caused by lack of vitamin C, found in citrus fruits.

q.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of:
q.e: Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions in living things.

q.q: Starch gives a blue-black colour with:
q.e: The iodine test detects starch.

q.q: The most abundant gas in the atmosphere is:
q.e: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

q.q: The ozone layer protects the earth from:
q.e: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV rays.

q.q: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are harmful because they:
q.e: CFCs release chlorine atoms that break down ozone.

q.q: Acid rain is mainly caused by:
q.e: SO2 and NOx from vehicles and factories form sulphuric and nitric acids in rain.

q.q: The greenhouse effect is increased mainly by rising levels of:
q.e: CO2, methane and water vapour trap heat, causing global warming.

q.q: Smog in Lahore during winter is mainly caused by:
o: smoke, vehicle exhaust and crop burning trapped near the ground
q.e: Pollutants from vehicles, industry and crop burning get trapped in cold air, forming smog.

q.q: The layer of the atmosphere closest to the earth is the:
q.e: We live in the troposphere, where weather happens.

q.q: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it:
o: reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen
q.e: CO binds to haemoglobin strongly, stopping oxygen transport.

q.q: Water that does not easily form lather with soap is called:
q.e: Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts that react with soap.

q.q: Temporary hardness of water can be removed by:
q.e: Boiling turns calcium hydrogencarbonate into insoluble calcium carbonate.

q.q: Permanent hardness is caused by:
o: sulphates and chlorides of calcium and magnesium
q.e: These salts are not removed by boiling; washing soda or ion exchange is used.

q.q: Water is a good solvent because it is:
q.e: Water molecules are polar, so they dissolve many ionic and polar substances.

q.q: Waterborne diseases include:
q.e: Drinking contaminated water spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and hepatitis.

q.q: Boiling drinking water at home mainly helps by:
q.e: Boiling kills most bacteria and viruses, making water safer to drink.

q.q: Industrial waste in rivers is harmful mainly because it:
o: adds toxic chemicals and heavy metals
q.e: Chemicals and metals like lead and mercury poison aquatic life and people.

q.q: The chemical formula of water is:
q.e: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

q.q: Urea is mainly used as a:
q.e: Urea is a nitrogen fertiliser widely used in Pakistan.

q.q: The Solvay process is used to make:
q.e: The Solvay process produces sodium carbonate from salt, limestone and ammonia.

q.q: Petroleum is separated into useful fractions by:
q.e: Fractions with different boiling points are separated in a fractionating column.

q.q: Ammonia used for making urea is produced by combining:
q.e: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3 (Haber process).

q.q: Petrol, diesel and kerosene are obtained from:
q.e: They are fractions of crude oil.

q.q: Washing soda (sodium carbonate) is used to:
q.e: Sodium carbonate is used in glass making, softening hard water and in detergents.

q.q: In humans, the exchange of gases takes place in the:
q.e: Alveoli have thin walls and many capillaries, so oxygen and CO2 diffuse easily.

q.q: During inhalation, the diaphragm:
q.e: Diaphragm contraction increases chest volume, lowering pressure so air rushes in.

q.q: In plants, gases enter and leave the leaf mainly through:
q.e: Stomata are tiny pores on leaves controlled by guard cells.

q.q: The gas released as a waste product of respiration is:
q.e: Cellular respiration produces CO2 and water, which we breathe out.

q.q: Smoking damages the lungs mainly because tobacco smoke:
o: contains tar and harmful chemicals that damage alveoli
q.e: Tar and chemicals damage alveoli and cilia, causing bronchitis, emphysema and lung cancer.

q.q: Pneumonia is an infection of the:
q.e: Pneumonia fills alveoli with fluid, making breathing difficult.

q.q: The structure that prevents food from entering the windpipe is the:
q.e: The epiglottis closes over the larynx when we swallow.

q.q: Plants release oxygen during the day mainly because:
q.e: In daylight photosynthesis produces more oxygen than respiration uses.

q.q: Homeostasis means:
o: keeping the internal environment of the body constant
q.e: Homeostasis keeps temperature, water and glucose levels steady.

q.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
q.e: Each kidney has about a million nephrons that filter blood and make urine.

q.q: The main nitrogenous waste in human urine is:
q.e: The liver converts excess amino acids to urea, which kidneys remove.

q.q: Kidney stones can form when:
o: salts crystallise in the urine, often due to low water intake
q.e: Drinking enough water helps prevent stones, especially in hot weather.

q.q: When the body is too hot, it cools down by:
q.e: Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the skin.

q.q: If both kidneys fail, a patient can be treated by:
q.e: Dialysis filters the blood artificially; a transplant replaces the kidney.

q.q: Plants get rid of extra water vapour mainly by:
q.e: Water evaporates through stomata in transpiration.

q.q: The organ that regulates blood glucose by producing insulin is the:
q.e: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood glucose.

q.q: The basic unit of the nervous system is the:
q.e: Neurons carry nerve impulses.

q.q: A reflex action is:
o: a quick, automatic response to a stimulus
q.e: Pulling your hand from a hot object happens before you think, through a reflex arc.

q.q: The part of the brain that controls balance and coordination is the:
q.e: The cerebellum coordinates muscles and balance.

q.q: Hormones are carried around the body by the:
q.e: Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the blood.

q.q: The "master gland" of the endocrine system is the:
q.e: The pituitary controls many other glands.

q.q: Lack of iodine in the diet can cause:
q.e: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine; deficiency swells the thyroid (goitre). Iodised salt prevents it.

q.q: The adrenaline hormone prepares the body for:
q.e: Adrenaline raises heart rate and blood sugar in emergencies.

q.q: The light-sensitive layer of the eye is the:
q.e: The retina has rods and cones that detect light.

q.q: The human skeleton has about:
q.e: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.

q.q: The joint at the knee and elbow is a:
q.e: Hinge joints allow movement in one plane, like a door hinge.

q.q: Muscles are attached to bones by:
q.e: Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

q.q: The biceps and triceps work as:
q.e: When one contracts the other relaxes, bending or straightening the arm.

q.q: Osteoporosis is a condition in which bones:
q.e: Loss of calcium makes bones fragile; calcium, vitamin D and exercise help prevent it.

q.q: Arthritis mainly affects the:
q.e: Arthritis is inflammation of joints, causing pain and stiffness.

q.q: The hip and shoulder joints are:
q.e: They allow movement in many directions.

q.q: Cartilage at the ends of bones:
q.e: Smooth cartilage cushions joints and lets bones move easily.

q.q: Reproduction involving one parent and no gametes is:
q.e: Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring.

q.q: Binary fission is a method of reproduction in:
q.e: The cell divides into two identical cells.

q.q: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called:
q.e: Pollination happens by wind, insects or water.

q.q: Growing new plants from stems, roots or leaves is called:
q.e: Potato tubers, rose cuttings and onion bulbs are examples.

q.q: The fusion of male and female gametes is called:
q.e: Fertilisation forms a zygote.

q.q: The male part of a flower is the:
q.e: The stamen has an anther (makes pollen) and a filament.

q.q: For germination, a seed needs:
o: water, oxygen and a suitable temperature
q.e: Most seeds need water, oxygen and warmth; light is not always needed.

q.q: AIDS is caused by:
q.e: HIV attacks the immune system and spreads through blood, unsafe sex and unsterile needles.

q.q: The basic unit of heredity is the:
q.e: Genes are segments of DNA that carry instructions for traits.

q.q: Normal human body cells contain:
q.e: Gametes have 23; fertilisation restores 46.

q.q: In Mendel's pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t). A plant with genotype Tt will be:
q.e: A dominant allele shows its effect even when only one copy is present.

q.q: Crossing Tt x Tt gives tall and dwarf plants in the ratio:
q.e: Offspring: TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Three tall to one dwarf.

q.q: The father of genetics is:
q.e: Mendel discovered the laws of inheritance using pea plants.

q.q: Variations among individuals of the same species are important because they:
q.e: Variation gives raw material for natural selection.

q.q: DNA is mainly found in the cell's:
q.e: Most DNA is in the chromosomes inside the nucleus.

q.q: The sex of a human baby is decided by the chromosome from the:
q.e: Mothers give an X; fathers give X (girl) or Y (boy).

q.q: All the living organisms and their physical environment together form an:
q.e: An ecosystem includes biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) parts.

q.q: Green plants in a food chain are called:
q.e: Producers make food by photosynthesis.

q.q: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead matter are:
q.e: Decomposers recycle nutrients back into the soil.

q.q: In the food chain grass -> goat -> lion, the goat is a:
q.e: The goat eats plants, so it is the primary consumer.

q.q: Deforestation leads to:
o: soil erosion and loss of habitat
q.e: Cutting forests removes roots that hold soil and destroys animal homes.

q.q: The energy in a food chain originally comes from the:
q.e: Plants capture sunlight energy in photosynthesis.

q.q: Planting trees helps the environment because trees:
q.e: Trees reduce greenhouse gases, give shade and protect soil.

q.q: Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next because the rest is:
o: lost as heat in respiration and activities
q.e: Most energy is used for life processes and lost as heat.

q.q: Using microorganisms to make useful products is called:
q.e: Examples: yoghurt, bread, antibiotics and insulin.

q.q: Yoghurt is made from milk by:
q.e: Lactobacillus converts lactose into lactic acid, thickening the milk.

q.q: Yeast makes bread dough rise by producing:
q.e: Yeast ferments sugar and releases CO2 bubbles.

q.q: Human insulin for diabetics is now produced by:
q.e: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria, which then make insulin.

q.q: Inserting a gene from one organism into another is called:
q.e: It produces genetically modified organisms (GMOs).

q.q: Single cell protein (SCP) refers to:
q.e: Microbes like yeast and algae can be grown as protein food or feed.

q.q: Drugs used to kill bacteria are called:
q.e: Antibiotics like penicillin kill or stop bacteria. They do not work on viruses.

q.q: Penicillin was discovered by:
q.e: Fleming discovered penicillin from a mould in 1928.

q.q: Vaccines protect us by:
o: training the immune system to recognise a germ
q.e: Vaccines contain weakened or dead germs or their parts, so the body makes antibodies in advance.

q.q: Taking antibiotics when they are not needed, or not finishing the course, can cause:
q.e: Bacteria that survive become resistant, making future infections hard to treat.

q.q: Narcotics such as heroin are dangerous mainly because they:
q.e: They cause dependence and serious physical and social harm.

q.q: Painkillers (analgesics) are used to:
q.e: Analgesics like paracetamol reduce pain; they should be taken as advised.

p: Base quantities: length (m), mass (kg), time (s), current (A), temperature (K), amount (mol), light intensity (cd).
Prefixes: kilo = 10^3, centi = 10^-2, milli = 10^-3, micro = 10^-6.
Vernier calliper measures to 0.1 mm; screw gauge to 0.01 mm.
Scientific notation: write numbers as a x 10^n with 1 <= a < 10.
Scalars have magnitude only (speed, distance); vectors also have direction (velocity, displacement).
Speed = distance / time; acceleration = change in velocity / time.
Slope of distance-time graph = speed; slope of velocity-time graph = acceleration; area under v-t graph = distance.
Equations of motion: vf = vi + at; S = vi t + 1/2 a t^2; 2aS = vf^2 - vi^2.
First law (inertia): no net force means no change in motion.
Second law: F = ma. Third law: action and reaction are equal and opposite.
Momentum p = m v; momentum is conserved in collisions.
Friction opposes motion; reduce it with lubricants and ball bearings.
Torque = force x perpendicular distance from the pivot.
Equilibrium: net force = 0 and net torque = 0.
Centre of gravity: point where the whole weight acts.
Lower centre of gravity and wider base give more stability.
Law of gravitation: F = G m1 m2 / r^2.
g on earth is about 9.8 m/s^2; on the moon about 1/6 of that.
Mass stays the same everywhere; weight W = m g changes.
Gravity keeps satellites and the moon in orbit.
Work W = F x d (joule).
Kinetic energy = 1/2 m v^2; potential energy = m g h.
Power = work / time (watt).
Energy is conserved; renewable sources: solar, wind, hydel.
Pressure P = F/A (pascal). Liquid pressure = rho g h.
Density = mass / volume; less dense objects float.
Pascal's law: pressure in an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally (hydraulic press).
Hooke's law: F = kx within the elastic limit.
Temperature measures average kinetic energy of molecules.
Solids, liquids and gases expand on heating (gaps in railway tracks).
Latent heat changes state without changing temperature; evaporation causes cooling.
Conduction: through solids, particle to particle. Convection: in fluids by moving currents. Radiation: no medium needed.
Metals conduct well; plastic, wood and air are insulators.
Dark rough surfaces absorb and emit heat well; shiny surfaces reflect.
Thermos flask reduces all three methods of heat transfer.
Like poles repel, unlike poles attract.
A freely suspended magnet points north-south (compass).
Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic.
Soft iron for temporary magnets (electromagnets); steel for permanent magnets.
Element: one kind of atom. Compound: elements chemically combined. Mixture: physically mixed.
Atomic mass and molar mass in g/mol; moles = mass / molar mass.
Avogadro's number = 6.02 x 10^23 particles per mole.
Proton (+) and neutron (0) in the nucleus; electrons (-) in shells.
Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons.
Isotopes: same protons, different neutrons. Shell capacity = 2n^2.
Modern periodic table: increasing atomic number. Groups (columns) and periods (rows).
Same group = same valence electrons = similar properties.
Across a period atomic size decreases; down a group it increases. Group 18: noble gases.
Atoms bond to get a stable octet.
Ionic bond: electron transfer (NaCl). Covalent bond: electron sharing (H2O, N2 triple bond).
Ionic compounds have high melting points and conduct when molten or dissolved.
Solids: fixed shape and volume; liquids: fixed volume; gases: neither.
Boyle's law PV = constant; Charles's law V/T = constant.
Diffusion is fastest in gases. Sublimation: solid to gas directly.
Solution = solute + solvent. Saturated holds the maximum solute.
Concentration % w/w = (solute / solution) x 100; molarity = moles / litres.
True solution, colloid (milk) and suspension (muddy water) differ by particle size.
Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain (OIL RIG).
Rusting needs water and oxygen; prevent by paint, oil, galvanising (zinc).
Electrolysis: anode is positive (oxidation), cathode is negative (reduction).
Metals lose electrons; non-metals gain electrons.
Reactivity: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, ... , Cu, Ag, Au (least).
Sodium reacts violently with water; gold is unreactive.
Biology is the study of life; branches include anatomy, physiology, ecology, genetics and palaeontology.
Levels: atom, molecule, cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.
Biology helps in medicine, agriculture and protecting the environment.
Scientific method: observation, hypothesis, experiment, results, conclusion.
A control group is used for fair comparison.
A theory is a well-tested explanation; a law describes what always happens.
Biodiversity is the variety of life.
Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature (genus + species).
Five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
Cell parts: nucleus (control), mitochondria (energy), ribosomes (proteins).
Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
Tissues are groups of similar cells.
Mitosis: two identical cells (growth and repair).
Meiosis: four cells with half the chromosomes (gametes).
Uncontrolled division can cause cancer.
Enzymes are protein catalysts with an active site.
They work best at an optimum temperature and pH; heat denatures them.
Lock and key model explains specificity.
Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6O2 (in chloroplasts).
Aerobic respiration releases more energy; anaerobic gives alcohol + CO2 (yeast) or lactic acid (muscles).
ATP is the energy currency of the cell.
Balanced diet: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, fibre.
Protein deficiency: kwashiorkor; iron deficiency: anaemia.
Digestion finishes in the small intestine; villi absorb food; liver makes bile.
Xylem carries water up; phloem carries food. Transpiration pulls water up.
Heart has four chambers; arteries carry blood away, veins bring it back, capillaries exchange materials.
Red cells (haemoglobin) carry oxygen; white cells fight infection; platelets help clotting.
Order = rows x columns. Add matrices of the same order.
Determinant of [[a, b], [c, d]] = ad - bc. Singular if it equals 0.
Inverse exists only for non-singular square matrices.
Rational numbers can be written as p/q; irrational ones (root 2, pi) cannot.
i = root(-1), i^2 = -1. Complex number: a + bi.
Conjugate of a + bi is a - bi.
If a^x = y then log_a y = x.
log(ab) = log a + log b; log(a/b) = log a - log b; log(a^n) = n log a.
log 1 = 0; log_a a = 1.
Take out common factors first.
x^2 + (a+b)x + ab = (x + a)(x + b).
Difference of squares: x^2 - a^2 = (x + a)(x - a).
HCF: highest common factor; LCM: lowest common multiple.
HCF x LCM = product of two numbers.
Square root of a perfect square expression: (x + 1)^2 gives x + 1.
Solve equations by doing the same to both sides.
In inequalities, multiplying by a negative number reverses the sign.
|x| = a means x = a or x = -a.
y = mx + c is a straight line: m is the slope, c is the y-intercept.
Points on the y-axis have x = 0; on the x-axis y = 0.
Plot at least two or three points to draw a line.
Distance = root((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2).
Quadrants: I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-).
Congruent triangles have the same shape and size.
Tests: SAS, ASA, SSS, RHS (AAA is not a test).
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal.
Parallelogram: opposite sides equal and parallel, opposite angles equal.
Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
The line joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half of it.
Points on a perpendicular bisector are equidistant from the segment's ends.
Perpendicular bisectors of a triangle meet at the circumcentre.
Angle bisectors of a triangle meet at the incentre.

notes.t: Sides and Angles of a Triangle
p: Angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.
The greater angle faces the longer side.
Sum of any two sides is greater than the third side.
Ratio compares quantities: a : b.
In a proportion a : b = c : d, product of extremes = product of means (ad = bc).
To divide in a ratio, find the total parts first.
f: a : b = c : d means ad = bc

p: In a right triangle, hypotenuse^2 = base^2 + perpendicular^2.
The converse tests whether a triangle is right-angled.
Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels have equal area.
Triangle area = 1/2 x base x height.
Triangles on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area.
Percentage means out of 100: x% of y = x/100 x y.
Discount is taken from the marked price.
Direct proportion: both increase together; inverse: one increases as the other decreases.
f: x% of y = x/100 x y

p: Zakat: 2.5% of eligible savings above nisab held for one lunar year.
Ushr: 10% of produce from rain-fed land, 5% from irrigated land.
Inheritance shares follow Islamic law (Quran).
Profit = selling price - cost price; loss = cost price - selling price.
Profit % = profit / cost price x 100.
Commission and taxes are calculated as percentages.
Simple interest I = P R T / 100.
Islamic banking uses profit and loss sharing instead of interest.
Compare saving options before deciding.
Bills: units x rate + taxes.
Instalment buying usually costs more than cash.
Budgeting helps plan income and spending.
a^m x a^n = a^(m+n); a^m / a^n = a^(m-n); (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
log is the inverse of an exponent: 10^2 = 100 means log 100 = 2.
Arithmetic sequence: add a common difference d. nth term = a + (n - 1)d.
Geometric sequence: multiply by a common ratio r. nth term = a r^(n-1).
Find the pattern before writing the next term.
A set is a collection of distinct objects.
Union: all elements of both sets; intersection: common elements.
A function gives exactly one output for each input.
Points on the x-axis have y = 0; on the y-axis x = 0.
Direct proportion gives a straight line through the origin.
Conversion graphs help change units (rupees, dollars, km, miles).
Mean = sum / number of values.
Median = middle value of ordered data.
Mode = most frequent value.
SHM: acceleration is towards the mean position and proportional to displacement (a = -kx).
Simple pendulum period: T = 2 pi root(l/g); it does not depend on mass or small amplitude.
Speed is maximum at the mean position and zero at the extremes; energy changes between KE and PE.
Waves carry energy, not matter. Transverse: particles move at right angles. Longitudinal: along the wave.
Amplitude = maximum displacement; frequency f = 1/T; wave speed v = f x wavelength.
Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave; it needs a medium and cannot travel in a vacuum.
Speed of sound: solids > liquids > gases (about 340 m/s in air).
Pitch depends on frequency; loudness on amplitude; quality (timbre) on waveform.
Human hearing: about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Below: infrasound. Above: ultrasound (medical scans, bats).
Echo: reflected sound; distance = v x t / 2. Soft materials absorb sound to reduce echoes.
Law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection (measured from the normal).
Refraction: light bends towards the normal entering a denser medium; n = c/v.
Total internal reflection: denser to rarer medium and angle greater than the critical angle. Used in optical fibres.
Convex lens converges light; concave lens diverges light. Power P = 1/f (dioptre, f in metres).
Myopia (short sight): concave lens. Hypermetropia (long sight): convex lens.
Like charges repel, unlike charges attract. Charging by rubbing moves electrons, never protons.
Coulomb's law: F = k q1 q2 / r squared; doubling distance gives 1/4 force.
Electric field lines go from positive to negative charge.
Capacitor stores charge; C = Q/V. Parallel: C = C1 + C2. Series: 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2.
Earthing and lightning conductors make static electricity safe.
Current I = Q/t (ampere). Potential difference measured in volts.
Ohm's law: V = IR. Resistance rises with length and temperature, falls with thickness.
Series: R = R1 + R2. Parallel: 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2.
Ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel. Homes are wired in parallel.
Energy (kWh) = power (kW) x time (h); 1 kWh = 1 unit. Fuse and earth wire protect against faults.
A current produces a magnetic field (Oersted). Right hand grip rule gives its direction.
Fleming's left hand rule: force on a current in a magnetic field (motor effect).
Electromagnetic induction: changing magnetic flux induces emf (generator, transformer).
Transformer: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np; works only with AC. Step-up raises voltage, step-down lowers it.
High-voltage transmission reduces current and energy loss.
f: Vp x Ip = Vs x Is (ideal)

p: Thermionic emission: heated metals emit electrons (used in CRO).
Analogue signals vary continuously; digital signals are 0 or 1.
AND: 1 only if all inputs are 1. OR: 0 only if all inputs are 0. NOT: inverts.
NAND = NOT AND; NOR = NOT OR.
Binary numbers use only 0 and 1 (5 = 101).
ICT = technologies to store, process and communicate information.
Radio waves carry mobile and radio signals; optical fibres carry light signals.
Storage: RAM is temporary; hard disk and flash memory are permanent.
The internet is a worldwide network of networks; e-mail sends messages and files.
Online safety: never share passwords or OTPs; beware of fake prize links.
Alpha: helium nucleus, stopped by paper. Beta: fast electron, stopped by aluminium. Gamma: EM wave, needs lead.
Beta decay raises atomic number by 1; alpha decay lowers it by 2 and mass number by 4.
Half-life: time for half the nuclei to decay; after n half-lives, (1/2)^n remains.
Background radiation is mostly natural (rocks, radon, cosmic rays).
Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion joins light nuclei. Radioisotopes are used in medicine and industry.
Reversible reactions go both ways; equilibrium is reached in a closed system.
At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal (dynamic equilibrium).
Kc = [products]/[reactants]; large Kc favours products, small Kc favours reactants.
Le Chatelier: a system shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure or temperature.
A catalyst does not change the equilibrium position; it only speeds up reaching it.
Arrhenius: acids give H+, bases give OH- in water.
Bronsted-Lowry: acid = proton donor, base = proton acceptor. Lewis: acid accepts an electron pair.
pH < 7 acidic, 7 neutral, > 7 basic. Strong acids (HCl) ionise fully; weak acids (vinegar) partly.
Neutralisation: acid + base -> salt + water.
Indicators: litmus red in acid, blue in base; phenolphthalein pink in base.
Organic compounds are carbon compounds; carbon shows catenation.
Isomers: same molecular formula, different structure.
Functional groups: -OH alcohol, -CHO aldehyde, >C=O ketone, -COOH carboxylic acid.
Homologous series: members differ by -CH2- and share properties.
Sources: coal, petroleum, natural gas, plants and animals.
Hydrocarbons contain only C and H.
Alkanes CnH2n+2 (saturated, single bonds); alkenes CnH2n (double bond); alkynes CnH2n-2 (triple bond).
Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water.
Complete combustion gives CO2 + H2O; incomplete gives poisonous CO.
Natural gas (Sui gas) is mainly methane; always ventilate rooms with gas heaters.
Carbohydrates (C, H, O): monosaccharides like glucose; polysaccharides like starch.
Proteins are made of amino acids; enzymes are proteins.
Lipids store energy; nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) carry genetic information.
Vitamins: C deficiency causes scurvy, D deficiency causes rickets, A deficiency causes night blindness.
Tests: iodine for starch, Benedict's for reducing sugars.
Air: about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, small amounts of argon and CO2.
Troposphere is the lowest layer; the ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs UV.
CFCs destroy ozone. CO2 and methane increase the greenhouse effect.
Acid rain comes from SO2 and NOx. Smog comes from smoke, exhaust and crop burning.
CO stops blood carrying oxygen; it is colourless and odourless.
Water is polar, so it is a good solvent.
Hard water has calcium and magnesium salts. Temporary hardness is removed by boiling; permanent hardness needs washing soda or ion exchange.
Waterborne diseases: cholera, typhoid, dysentery, hepatitis.
Boiling and filtering make drinking water safer.
Industrial waste adds toxic chemicals and heavy metals to water.
Urea is a nitrogen fertiliser made from ammonia and CO2.
Haber process: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3.
Solvay process makes sodium carbonate (washing soda) used in glass and softening water.
Crude oil is separated by fractional distillation into petrol, diesel, kerosene and more.
Chemical industries are important for Pakistan's agriculture and economy.
Human gas exchange happens in alveoli (thin walls, many capillaries).
Inhalation: diaphragm contracts and moves down, ribs move out; exhalation is the reverse.
Plants exchange gases through stomata.
Respiration produces CO2; in daylight plants give out more O2 than they use.
Smoking damages alveoli and cilia; pneumonia and bronchitis affect the lungs.
Homeostasis keeps temperature, water and glucose constant.
Kidneys filter blood in nephrons; urea is the main waste in urine.
Sweating cools the body; shivering warms it.
Kidney failure: dialysis or transplant. Drink enough water to prevent stones.
Pancreas makes insulin to lower blood glucose; plants lose water by transpiration.
Neurons carry impulses; reflex actions are fast and automatic.
Cerebrum: thinking; cerebellum: balance; medulla: breathing and heartbeat.
Hormones travel in blood; pituitary is the master gland.
Iodine deficiency causes goitre; adrenaline prepares for fight or flight.
Eye: retina detects light; ear helps hearing and balance.
Adult skeleton: 206 bones; it supports, protects and helps movement.
Joints: hinge (knee, elbow), ball and socket (hip, shoulder), fixed (skull).
Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.
Biceps and triceps are an antagonistic pair.
Osteoporosis weakens bones; arthritis inflames joints.
Asexual reproduction: one parent, identical offspring (binary fission, budding, vegetative propagation).
Sexual reproduction: gametes fuse in fertilisation to form a zygote.
Flower: stamen is male (anther, filament); carpel is female (stigma, style, ovary).
Pollination moves pollen to the stigma; germination needs water, oxygen and warmth.
HIV causes AIDS; it spreads through blood, unsafe sex and unsterile needles.
Genes on chromosomes (DNA) carry traits; humans have 46 chromosomes.
Mendel: dominant alleles mask recessive ones; Tt x Tt gives a 3 : 1 ratio.
Genotype = genes (TT, Tt, tt); phenotype = how the organism looks.
Sex is decided by the father's X or Y chromosome.
Variation helps species survive and evolve.
Ecosystem = living things + their physical environment.
Food chain: producers -> primary consumers -> secondary consumers; decomposers recycle.
Energy comes from the sun; about 10% passes to the next level.
Deforestation causes soil erosion and habitat loss; trees absorb CO2.
Pollution and overpopulation harm ecosystems.
Biotechnology uses living things to make useful products.
Lactobacillus makes yoghurt; yeast makes bread rise (CO2) and ferments sugar.
Genetic engineering inserts genes into other organisms (insulin from bacteria).
Single cell protein is food made from microbes.
Fermentation is used for foods, medicines and fuels.
Antibiotics kill bacteria (not viruses); Fleming discovered penicillin.
Vaccines train the immune system in advance.
Misusing antibiotics causes resistance; always complete the course.
Painkillers relieve pain; narcotics are addictive and harmful.
Take medicines only as advised by a doctor.
